title: Series-Parallel Hybrid SOT-MRAM Computing-in-Memory Macro with Multi-Method Modulation for High Area and Energy Efficiency
problem: Existing MRAM-series and MRAM-parallel architectures for computing-in-memory suffer from high energy costs and low flexibility, respectively, limiting their applicability for neural network inference.
motivation: Computing-in-memory demonstrates superiority for neural network inference; exploring SOT-MRAM-based CIM implementations can provide better area and energy efficiency.
method: The chip stores weights and performs calculations in magnetic memory cells on the same piece of silicon—a computing-in-memory approach that eliminates the energy waste of shuttling data between memory and processors. The design uses a weight group architecture made of 6 transistors paired with 4 magnetic junctions that can operate in either series mode (junctions stacked end-to-end for efficiency) or parallel mode (junctions side-by-side for flexibility), with a hybrid layout supporting both. A configurable modulation scheme lets you adjust the precision per operation (2, 4, 6, or 8 bits) depending on what accuracy you need, optimizing power consumption. The design was built and validated in both 180-nanometer and 28-nanometer process technologies.
key_novelty: The innovation is a hybrid architecture that combines series and parallel magnetic junction configurations in one structure, achieving the energy efficiency of pure series designs and the architectural flexibility of pure parallel designs.
contributions: Series-parallel hybrid architecture for SOT-MRAM CIM addressing energy-flexibility trade-offs
Multi-method modulation scheme with configurable 2-8 bit input precision
Implementation and verification in 180nm and 28nm technology nodes
Achieved energy efficiency of 23.7-29.6 Tops/W at 8-bit precision
primary_theme: SOT-MRAM CIM macro with hybrid MTJ architecture
